# Phenomenological Implications of Large tan(β) in the MSSM

## Introduction and Motivation

This paper investigates the rich phenomenological landscape that emerges within the Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model (MSSM) when the ratio of the two Higgs doublet vacuum expectation values, tan(β), is taken to be large. This regime is particularly compelling from a theoretical standpoint, as it arises naturally in various models of supersymmetry breaking and grand unification, and it induces significant modifications to Yukawa couplings and loop-level contributions that can leave observable imprints across multiple sectors of particle physics. The large tan(β) scenario enhances certain non-standard couplings, particularly those involving the Higgs sector and chargino/neutralino loops, making it an especially fertile ground for probing physics beyond the Standard Model (BSM). We systematically examine three complementary avenues through which such new physics signatures may manifest: leptonic flavor violation, hadronic flavor violation, and violations of lepton universality in charged current interactions.

## Leptonic Flavor Violating Processes

A central focus of this work is the review of Leptonic Flavor Violating (LFV) processes, which represent one of the most sensitive probes of new physics beyond the Standard Model. In the Standard Model, lepton flavor is conserved to an excellent approximation (up to negligible effects from neutrino masses), meaning that any observation of processes such as μ → eγ, τ → μγ, τ → eγ, or related three-body decays (μ → 3e, τ → 3μ, etc.) would constitute an unambiguous signal of new physics. Within the large tan(β) regime of the MSSM, these LFV processes receive potentially large contributions from loop diagrams involving sleptons, charginos, and neutralinos, with the amplitudes often scaling with positive powers of tan(β). We review the theoretical framework underlying these calculations, discuss the relevant effective operators, and examine how current experimental bounds on LFV branching ratios translate into constraints on the MSSM parameter space, particularly on slepton mass matrices and flavor-violating soft SUSY-breaking terms. The complementarity between different LFV channels is also addressed, highlighting how simultaneous consideration of multiple processes can help disentangle the underlying new physics structure.

## Hadronic Flavor Violating Processes

Parallel to the leptonic sector, we conduct a thorough analysis of Hadronic Flavor Violating (HFV) processes, which offer an equally powerful and complementary window into physics beyond the Standard Model. These processes encompass a variety of phenomena including B meson mixing (Bs and Bd systems), rare B decays such as Bs → μ+μ− and B → Xsγ, as well as K meson observables. In the large tan(β) regime, Higgs-mediated flavor-changing neutral current (FCNC) contributions become particularly relevant, as the enhanced Yukawa couplings can generate sizable effects in processes that are otherwise highly suppressed in the Standard Model. We discuss how these hadronic observables provide stringent constraints on the MSSM parameter space, often complementary to those derived from direct collider searches, and we highlight the interplay between hadronic and leptonic flavor observables in constraining specific realizations of supersymmetry breaking, such as minimal flavor violation (MFV) versus more general flavor structures.

## Tests of Lepton Universality

Finally, we demonstrate that tests of Lepton Universality (LU) in charged current processes constitute a valuable and complementary tool for probing new physics scenarios within this framework. Lepton universality, a fundamental prediction of the Standard Model's gauge structure, posits that the coupling strengths of the W boson (and other gauge bosons) to different lepton generations are identical, up to calculable mass-dependent phase space corrections. We examine how large tan(β) effects in the MSSM can induce apparent violations of this universality, particularly in processes such as leptonic and semileptonic meson decays (e.g., π → μν versus π → eν, or K → μν versus K → eν), as well as in tau decays. These effects typically arise from charged Higgs boson exchange, whose couplings are tan(β)-enhanced for down-type fermions. We show how precision measurements of ratios sensitive to lepton universality violation can be used to place competitive constraints on the charged Higgs mass and tan(β), often providing bounds that are complementary to, and sometimes more stringent than, those obtained from direct collider searches or other flavor observables.

## Conclusion

Taken together, these three classes of observables—leptonic flavor violation, hadronic flavor violation, and lepton universality violation—provide a comprehensive and synergistic toolkit for exploring the phenomenological consequences of large tan(β) scenarios in the MSSM. This paper aims to present a cohesive review of these interconnected probes, emphasizing their combined power in constraining supersymmetric parameter space and their potential to reveal, or further constrain, the presence of new physics beyond the Standard Model.

# Phenomenological Implications of Large tan(β) in the MSSM: Lepton Universality and Flavor Violation as Probes of New Physics

## 1. Introduction

The Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model (MSSM) remains one of the most compelling extensions of the Standard Model (SM), offering elegant solutions to the hierarchy problem, gauge coupling unification, and providing a natural dark matter candidate. Among the various regions of MSSM parameter space, the large tan(β) regime—where tan(β) represents the ratio of the vacuum expectation values of the two Higgs doublets—occupies a particularly interesting position due to its rich phenomenological consequences. In this regime, tan(β) can take values ranging from approximately 30 to 50 or higher, leading to significant enhancements in certain Yukawa couplings and loop-induced effects that would otherwise be negligible in the SM or in the moderate tan(β) region of the MSSM.

This study undertakes a comprehensive analysis of the phenomenological implications arising from the large tan(β) regime, with particular emphasis on flavor violating (FV) processes as sensitive probes of physics beyond the Standard Model (BSM). Both leptonic and hadronic sectors are examined, as they offer complementary and synergistic constraints on the underlying supersymmetric parameter space.

## 2. Theoretical Framework

### 2.1 The Large tan(β) Regime

In the MSSM, the ratio tan(β) = v_u/v_d controls the relative strength of the up-type and down-type Yukawa couplings. When tan(β) becomes large, several important effects emerge:

- **Enhanced Yukawa couplings**: The bottom quark and tau lepton Yukawa couplings, which are proportional to tan(β), become comparable in magnitude to the top quark Yukawa coupling, potentially achieving Yukawa unification at high energy scales.

- **Non-decoupling effects**: Loop corrections involving supersymmetric particles do not decouple even for heavy superpartner masses, leading to potentially large deviations from SM predictions in flavor-changing processes.

- **Effective Lagrangian corrections**: The resummation of tan(β)-enhanced corrections becomes necessary, as fixed-order perturbation theory breaks down when tan(β) × (loop factor) approaches unity.

### 2.2 Flavor Violation as a Probe

Flavor violating processes provide a unique window into physics beyond the Standard Model because they are highly suppressed in the SM by the GIM mechanism and small Cabibbo-Kobayashi-Maskawa (CKM) matrix elements. In the MSSM at large tan(β), new sources of flavor violation can arise from:

- Non-minimal flavor structures in the soft SUSY-breaking sector
- Charged Higgs boson exchange with tan(β)-enhanced couplings
- Chargino/neutralino loop contributions to flavor-changing neutral currents
- Radiative corrections to fermion mass matrices

## 3. Leptonic Flavor Violation

### 3.1 Charged Lepton Flavor Violating Processes

The study extensively examines charged lepton flavor violation (LFV) processes, including:

- **μ → eγ**: This radiative decay serves as one of the most stringent probes of LFV, with current experimental bounds reaching branching ratios below 10⁻¹³.

- **τ → μγ and τ → eγ**: These tau-sector analogues provide complementary constraints, particularly sensitive to different regions of the SUSY parameter space.

- **μ → 3e and τ → 3ℓ**: Three-body decays proceeding through both photonic and non-photonic (box and Z-penguin) diagrams offer additional discriminating power.

- **μ-e conversion in nuclei**: This process, occurring through coherent conversion in the field of a nucleus, provides sensitivity to different operator structures compared to radiative decays.

At large tan(β), these processes receive significant contributions from double Higgs penguin diagrams and slepton mixing effects, particularly when the soft SUSY-breaking slepton mass matrices contain non-trivial off-diagonal terms.

### 3.2 Connection to Neutrino Physics

The observation of neutrino oscillations necessitates non-zero neutrino masses and lepton mixing, which in supersymmetric frameworks (particularly with seesaw mechanisms) naturally induces slepton mixing through renormalization group running. This connection provides a theoretical motivation for expecting observable LFV rates in well-motivated MSSM scenarios with large tan(β).

## 4. Hadronic Flavor Violation

### 4.1 B-Meson Physics

The hadronic sector analysis focuses substantially on B-meson observables, which have historically provided some of the most powerful constraints on large tan(β) scenarios:

- **B_s → μ⁺μ⁻**: This rare decay is particularly sensitive to tan(β)⁶ enhancement in certain MSSM scenarios, making it one of the most powerful probes of the large tan(β) regime.

- **B → τν**: Tree-level charged Higgs exchange contributes to this leptonic decay, with effects that can either enhance or suppress the SM prediction depending on the sign of μ (the Higgsino mass parameter).

- **b → sγ**: This radiative decay receives contributions from charged Higgs and chargino loops, providing constraints that are complementary to those from B_s → μ⁺μ⁻.

- **B_s - B̄_s mixing**: The mass difference ΔM_s receives contributions from double Higgs penguin diagrams that scale with tan(β)⁴, offering additional sensitivity to the large tan(β) parameter space.

### 4.2 Kaon Physics

Constraints from the kaon sector, while generally less sensitive to tan(β) enhancement than B-physics observables, still provide valuable complementary information, particularly regarding:

- K → πνν̄ decays
- ε'/ε and CP violation parameters
- K_L - K_S mass difference

## 5. Lepton Universality Tests in Charged Current Processes

### 5.1 Theoretical Motivation

A central and novel result of this analysis concerns the role of lepton universality (LU) tests within charged current processes. In the SM, gauge interactions are strictly universal across lepton generations—the coupling strength of the W boson to leptons is identical for electrons, muons, and tau leptons, up to calculable phase space and mass effects. Any observed deviation from this universality would constitute a clear signal of new physics.

In the MSSM at large tan(β), several mechanisms can induce apparent violations of lepton universality:

- **Charged Higgs contributions**: The charged Higgs boson couples to fermions with strength proportional to their masses times tan(β) (for down-type) or cot(β) (for up-type), leading to generation-dependent corrections to charged current amplitudes.

- **Loop-induced vertex corrections**: SUSY loop contributions to the W-lepton-neutrino vertex can differ between generations due to differing slepton and sneutrino masses/mixings.

- **Non-universal Yukawa coupling effects**: Radiative corrections proportional to tan(β) can differently affect the effective couplings of tau leptons compared to muons and electrons.

### 5.2 Specific Processes and Observables

The analysis examines several key ratios and processes sensitive to lepton universality violation:

- **R_τ/μ and R_τ/e**: Ratios of tau decay rates to muon/electron decay rates, particularly in leptonic tau decays (τ → ℓνν̄)

- **Pion and kaon leptonic decays**: R_K = Γ(K → eν)/Γ(K → μν), which is remarkably precisely predicted in the SM and highly sensitive to charged Higgs contributions

- **W boson leptonic branching ratios**: Direct measurements of W → ℓν branching fractions for different lepton flavors at hadron colliders

- **Tau polarization measurements**: Providing additional handles on potential non-universal couplings

### 5.3 Key Findings

The analysis reveals that lepton universality tests offer several distinct advantages as probes of new physics in the large tan(β) MSSM scenario:

1. **Theoretical cleanliness**: Many LU observables benefit from significant cancellation of hadronic uncertainties when taken as ratios, allowing for precision tests that are theoretically well-controlled.

2. **Complementarity**: LU violation signals probe different combinations of MSSM parameters compared to traditional flavor violation observables, breaking degeneracies that might otherwise obscure the interpretation of anomalies.

3. **Sensitivity to charged Higgs mass**: Several LU observables, particularly R_K, provide constraints on the charged Higgs mass and tan(β) that are competitive with, and in some parameter regions superior to, direct collider searches.

4. **Correlation with flavor violation**: The study establishes important correlations between potential LU violations and flavor violating processes, suggesting that a coherent BSM signal might manifest simultaneously across multiple observables if new physics is indeed present at accessible scales.

## 6. Implications for Future Experimental Searches

The findings of this study carry significant implications for the design and interpretation of future experimental programs:

### 6.1 High-Intensity Frontier Experiments

Future high-intensity experiments, including upgraded facilities for rare kaon and muon decay searches (such as next-generation μ → eγ and μ-e conversion experiments), will provide increasingly stringent tests of the large tan(β) MSSM scenario. The complementarity between LFV and LU observables suggests that a combined analysis strategy will be essential for fully exploiting the discovery potential of these experiments.

### 6.2 B-Factory and LHCb Prospects

Continued precision measurements at Belle II and LHCb will refine constraints on B_s → μ⁺μ⁻, B → τν, and related observables, further constraining the large tan(β) parameter space. The interplay between these hadronic flavor observables and lepton universality tests provides a powerful multi-pronged approach to either discovering or further constraining SUSY effects.

### 6.3 Precision Electroweak Measurements

The study emphasizes that precision measurements of lepton universality in W and tau decays, achievable at both existing and planned facilities, should be considered a priority alongside traditional flavor violation searches. These measurements offer theoretically clean signatures that can definitively establish or exclude regions of the large tan(β) MSSM parameter space.

## 7. Conclusions

This comprehensive analysis demonstrates that the large tan(β) regime of the MSSM gives rise to a rich phenomenology accessible through both leptonic and hadronic flavor violating processes. While traditional FV observables such as μ → eγ, B_s → μ⁺μ⁻, and b → sγ remain powerful probes of this parameter space, the study's principal contribution lies in establishing lepton universality tests in charged current processes as an equally valuable and complementary tool for constraining new physics scenarios.

The theoretical cleanliness of LU observables, combined with their distinct sensitivity to MSSM parameters compared to conventional flavor violation signals, positions them as essential components of the broader experimental strategy for probing supersymmetry at large tan(β). As experimental precision continues to improve across multiple frontiers—from high-intensity fixed-target experiments to B-factories and future collider facilities—the synergistic combination of flavor violation and lepton universality tests promises to significantly enhance our sensitivity to new physics, potentially providing crucial evidence for or against the large tan(β) MSSM scenario in the coming years.

The results underscore the importance of maintaining a broad and coordinated experimental program that encompasses both traditional flavor violation searches and precision lepton universality tests, as this comprehensive approach offers the best prospects for either confirming supersymmetric extensions of the Standard Model or further constraining viable regions of MSSM parameter space.

# The Flavor Structure of the MSSM

The Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model (MSSM) represents one of the most extensively studied extensions of the Standard Model, offering elegant solutions to several theoretical puzzles while introducing new challenges of its own—chief among them being the flavor problem.

## The Flavor Problem in Supersymmetry

In the Standard Model, the flavor structure is remarkably constrained: Yukawa couplings determine fermion masses and mixing angles, and the GIM mechanism naturally suppresses flavor-changing neutral currents (FCNCs). However, when supersymmetry is introduced, this delicate structure faces significant complications.

The MSSM introduces superpartners for every Standard Model particle, including squarks and sleptons. Crucially, the mass matrices for these scalar superpartners are not automatically aligned with the fermion Yukawa matrices. This misalignment opens the door to new sources of flavor violation that are largely absent or highly suppressed in the Standard Model.

## Sources of Flavor Violation

Several mechanisms can generate problematic flavor-violating effects in the MSSM:

**Soft SUSY-breaking terms**: The soft-breaking sector introduces mass matrices for squarks and sleptons that, in general, are not diagonal in the same basis as the corresponding fermion masses. This generic misalignment can induce large flavor-changing processes through gluino, neutralino, and chargino loops.

**Trilinear couplings**: The so-called A-terms, which couple scalars to Higgs fields, represent another potential source of flavor violation if they are not proportional to the Yukawa matrices.

**Renormalization group running**: Even if flavor universality is imposed at some high scale (as in minimal supergravity scenarios), renormalization group evolution down to the electroweak scale can reintroduce flavor-violating terms, particularly through Yukawa coupling effects in the running.

## Phenomenological Constraints

Experimental observations place stringent constraints on this flavor structure. Processes such as:

- $K^0-\bar{K}^0$ mixing
- $B_s-\bar{B}_s$ mixing  
- $\mu \to e\gamma$ decay
- Electric dipole moments

all provide powerful probes of new physics in the flavor sector. The absence of large deviations from Standard Model predictions in these observables imposes what is known as the "SUSY flavor problem"—the requirement that superpartner masses be either highly degenerate, aligned with Yukawa structures, or sufficiently heavy to suppress dangerous contributions.

## Solutions and Frameworks

Various theoretical frameworks have been proposed to address these constraints:

1. **Minimal Flavor Violation (MFV)**: Assumes that Yukawa couplings are the only source of flavor violation, even in the SUSY-breaking sector, thereby recovering approximate GIM-like protection.

2. **Gauge-mediated SUSY breaking**: Naturally produces flavor-universal soft terms since the mediation mechanism is flavor-blind.

3. **Alignment models**: Propose that squark mass matrices are aligned with Yukawa matrices due to underlying flavor symmetries.

4. **Decoupling solutions**: Simply push sfermion masses to very high scales, suppressing FCNC contributions at the cost of some fine-tuning.

## Conclusion

The interplay between flavor physics and supersymmetry breaking remains a central theme in understanding the viability and structure of the MSSM. Any realistic supersymmetric extension of the Standard Model must carefully address these flavor constraints, making this an essential ingredient in both model-building efforts and experimental searches for supersymmetric particles at colliders like the LHC.

# Abstract

We investigate large tan(β) effects in the Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model (MSSM) and their implications for flavor physics and lepton universality tests. In regions of parameter space where tan(β) is large, non-holomorphic corrections to the down-type quark and charged lepton Yukawa couplings become significant, generating effective flavor-changing neutral current (FCNC) couplings of the neutral Higgs bosons even in the absence of tree-level flavor violation. These corrections, resummed to all orders in tan(β), substantially modify predictions for B-meson observables, including B_s → μ⁺μ⁻, B → τν, and B–B̄ mixing, providing sensitive probes of supersymmetric parameter space complementary to direct collider searches.

We further examine how these tan(β)-enhanced loop corrections affect lepton universality in leptonic and semileptonic decays, particularly in channels involving τ leptons, such as B → Dτν, D_s → τν, and K → μν versus π → μν comparisons. The non-universal corrections to lepton-Higgs couplings can induce apparent violations of lepton flavor universality at the percent level, potentially accounting for anomalies observed in precision flavor measurements. We present a systematic framework for computing these effects using effective Lagrangian methods, incorporating both chargino-squark and gluino-squark loop contributions, and discuss the interplay between low-energy flavor observables, electroweak precision data, and Higgs boson phenomenology at the LHC. Our results demonstrate that large tan(β) scenarios in the MSSM predict correlated deviations across multiple flavor observables, offering a coherent set of signatures that could reveal or constrain supersymmetric extensions of the Standard Model even when superpartners lie beyond direct production thresholds at current colliders.

# Abstract

We investigate the impact of large tan(β) on flavor-violating processes in supersymmetric extensions of the Standard Model, focusing on both leptonic and hadronic sectors. In the large tan(β) regime, non-holomorphic Yukawa couplings generated through loop-induced corrections lead to enhanced flavor-changing neutral current (FCNC) effects that scale with positive powers of tan(β), potentially compensating for the suppression associated with heavy superpartner masses. We systematically analyze the dominant contributions to lepton flavor violating decays such as μ→eγ, μ→3e, and τ→μγ, alongside hadronic processes including B_s→μ⁺μ⁻, B→X_sγ, and K-meson mixing observables, within a general framework incorporating non-minimal flavor violation in the soft supersymmetry-breaking sector. Our analysis demonstrates that Higgs-mediated flavor-violating couplings, arising from misalignment between fermion mass matrices and their corresponding Yukawa structures, generate observable effects in both sectors that are correlated through the underlying supersymmetric flavor structure. We derive updated constraints on the relevant soft-breaking parameters using current experimental bounds from MEG, Belle II, and LHCb, and identify regions of parameter space where large tan(β) scenarios remain viable while predicting signals accessible to next-generation experiments. Particular attention is given to the interplay between chargino-neutralino and gluino-mediated contributions, which exhibit distinct tan(β) dependencies and can be disentangled through combined leptonic and hadronic flavor observables. Our results suggest that precision measurements in both sectors provide complementary and highly sensitive probes of supersymmetric flavor structure, with implications for the minimal supergravity, gauge-mediated, and more general soft-breaking scenarios at large tan(β).

# Phenomenology of Large tan(β) Scenarios in the MSSM

## Theoretical Framework

The Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model (MSSM) requires two Higgs doublets, whose vacuum expectation values $v_u$ and $v_d$ give rise to the parameter $\tan\beta \equiv v_u/v_d$. This ratio governs the relative strength of up-type and down-type Yukawa couplings and represents one of the most phenomenologically consequential free parameters of the model. Scenarios with large $\tan\beta$ (typically $\tan\beta \gtrsim 30$–50) are theoretically motivated by considerations of Yukawa coupling unification in grand unified theories, particularly $SO(10)$-inspired constructions where top and bottom Yukawa couplings are related at the GUT scale.

## Key Phenomenological Consequences

**Enhanced Yukawa Couplings and Radiative Corrections**

At large $\tan\beta$, the bottom-quark and tau-lepton Yukawa couplings become comparable in magnitude to the top-quark coupling, since $y_b \propto m_b/(v\cos\beta)$ receives a $\tan\beta$ enhancement. This has several consequences:

- Non-decoupling SUSY-QCD and electroweak corrections to the relation between $m_b$ and $y_b$ (the $\Delta_b$ resummation) become $O(1)$ effects, requiring careful treatment beyond fixed-order perturbation theory.
- The lightest CP-even Higgs mass receives large radiative corrections sensitive to stop masses and mixing, but the heavier Higgs states ($H^0$, $A^0$, $H^\pm$) develop enhanced couplings to down-type fermions $\propto \tan\beta$.

**Flavor-Changing Neutral Currents and Rare Decays**

Large $\tan\beta$ scenarios generate potentially large contributions to:

- $B_s \to \mu^+\mu^-$: branching ratio scales as $\tan^6\beta/M_A^4$ through double Higgs-penguin diagrams, making this observable a sensitive probe.
- $b \to s\gamma$: chargino-stop and charged Higgs loop contributions are $\tan\beta$-enhanced.
- $B \to \tau\nu$ and $B \to D\tau\nu$: tree-level charged Higgs exchange competes with $W$-boson exchange, with effects scaling as $\tan^2\beta/M_{H^\pm}^2$.

**Charged Higgs and Heavy Neutral Higgs Phenomenology**

The charged Higgs boson couples to fermions with strength $\propto (m_d \tan\beta, m_u \cot\beta)$ for down- and up-type quarks respectively, and $\propto m_\ell \tan\beta$ for leptons. This yields enhanced $H^\pm \to \tau\nu$ and $H^\pm \to tb$ signatures at colliders, while heavy neutral Higgses acquire enhanced couplings to $b\bar{b}$ and $\tau^+\tau^-$, motivating searches in $gg \to \phi \to \tau\tau$ and $b\bar{b}\phi$ production.

## Lepton Universality as a Probe of New Physics

Lepton flavor universality (LFU), a consequence of the equal gauge couplings of leptons to electroweak bosons in the Standard Model, provides a particularly clean and theoretically robust probe of large $\tan\beta$ MSSM effects, since New Physics contributions involving Yukawa-suppressed couplings naturally violate universality in a calculable manner.

**Charged Current Processes**

- **$\tau \to \mu\nu\bar\nu$ vs. $\mu \to e\nu\bar\nu$**: Charged Higgs exchange in tree-level leptonic decays introduces $\tan\beta$-dependent corrections proportional to $m_\ell^2 \tan^2\beta/M_{H^\pm}^2$, testable via ratios $g_\tau/g_\mu$ and $g_\mu/g_e$ extracted from precision measurements at B-factories and dedicated $\tau$ experiments.

- **$B \to D^{(*)}\tau\nu$ vs. $B \to D^{(*)}\ell\nu$** ($\ell = e,\mu$): The ratios $R(D)$ and $R(D^*)$ are sensitive to charged Higgs exchange, which modifies only the $\tau$ channel appreciably due to the Yukawa-enhanced coupling. Persistent tensions between measured values and SM predictions have been interpreted as potential hints of large $\tan\beta$ effects, though type-II 2HDM/MSSM charged Higgs contributions alone struggle to simultaneously accommodate both $R(D)$ and $R(D^*)$ anomalies without additional structure.

- **$K \to \mu\nu$ / $K \to e\nu$ and $\pi \to \mu\nu$/$\pi\to e\nu$**: These provide stringent low-energy tests, though charged Higgs contributions are suppressed by light quark masses.

**Neutral Current and Z-pole Observables**

- Supersymmetric loop corrections to $Z \to \ell^+\ell^-$ vertices, particularly through slepton-neutralino/chargino loops, can induce mild non-universal shifts, most relevant when third-generation sleptons are non-degenerate with first/second generation due to Yukawa-driven RGE running at large $\tan\beta$.

**Global Fits and Constraints**

Modern analyses combine LFU observables ($R(D^{(*)})$, $R_{K^{(*)}}$ in $b\to s\ell\ell$ transitions, $\tau$ and $\mu$ decay ratios) with direct collider limits on $M_{H^\pm}$ and $\tan\beta$ from LHC searches for $H^\pm \to \tau\nu$ and $H^\pm \to tb$. These fits generically disfavor the simplest large-$\tan\beta$ MSSM charged Higgs interpretation of $B$-physics anomalies for light-to-moderate $M_{H^\pm}$, pushing viable parameter space to heavier charged Higgs masses or motivating extensions to non-minimal flavor structures.

## Conclusion

Large $\tan\beta$ scenarios in the MSSM generate a rich and highly correlated phenomenology connecting Higgs sector physics, flavor observables, and precision electroweak tests. Lepton universality violation, as a low-background, theoretically clean signature, remains one of the most powerful indirect probes of these scenarios, complementing direct collider searches for heavy Higgs states and constraining the allowed $(\tan\beta, M_A)$ or $(\tan\beta, M_{H^\pm})$ parameter space in conjunction with flavor physics observables such as $B_s\to\mu^+\mu^-$ and $b\to s\gamma$.

# Abstract

The large tan(β) regime of the Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model (MSSM) offers a particularly rich phenomenology, where enhanced Yukawa couplings amplify the sensitivity of low-energy observables to supersymmetric dynamics. In this regime, non-holomorphic corrections to fermion masses—generated at the loop level and resummed to all orders in tan(β)—induce potentially large flavor-violating effects even in scenarios with minimal flavor violation at the messenger scale. These corrections modify Higgs-fermion couplings, generate effective flavor-changing neutral currents, and can produce sizable contributions to processes such as $B_s \to \mu^+\mu^-$, $B \to \tau\nu$, and $B$–$\bar{B}$ mixing, providing stringent constraints on the MSSM parameter space, particularly on the charged Higgs mass and $\tan\beta$ itself.

In this talk, I will review how these large tan(β) effects reshape the flavor structure of the MSSM, focusing on the interplay between squark/slepton flavor violation and constraints from $B$- and $K$-physics. I will then turn to lepton universality as a complementary and increasingly precise probe of new physics: charged-current processes such as $R_{\tau/\mu}$ in kaon and pion decays, as well as $R_{D^{(*)}}$-type ratios, offer sensitive tests of non-universal Higgs and slepton couplings induced by large tan(β) dynamics. I will discuss how current experimental precision on lepton flavor universality observables constrains the MSSM parameter space, highlighting complementarities and tensions between flavor-violation bounds and universality tests. Finally, I will comment on the prospects for disentangling genuine supersymmetric large tan(β) effects from other new physics scenarios using forthcoming data from LHCb, Belle II, and precision kaon experiments.

# Abstract

We investigate the phenomenology of flavor-changing neutral current (FCNC) processes and charged current lepton universality in the Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model (MSSM) in the large tan(β) regime. In this scenario, non-holomorphic corrections to the down-type quark and charged lepton Yukawa couplings become significant, generating tan(β)-enhanced contributions to Higgs-mediated flavor-violating amplitudes. We analyze the impact of these effects on B meson observables, including B_s → μ⁺μ⁻ and B → τν, as well as constraints arising from K meson mixing and rare decays. Particular attention is given to charged Higgs boson contributions to leptonic and semileptonic decays, which can induce apparent violations of charged current lepton universality in processes such as π → eν/π → μν and τ → eν̄ν/τ → μν̄ν ratios, as well as in R_τ = Γ(τ→ Kν)/Γ(τ→πν). We derive updated bounds on the charged Higgs mass and tan(β) parameter space from combined fits to precision electroweak and flavor data, and discuss the interplay between these constraints and supersymmetric particle spectra. Our results demonstrate that large tan(β) scenarios, while natural in many SUSY-breaking mediation schemes, are subject to stringent phenomenological constraints from lepton universality tests, providing complementary probes to direct collider searches for supersymmetric Higgs bosons.
